messages:
Elena (Finance): Quick broadcast: small update to PO & renewal handling rolling out Monday May 26. Goal: fewer emergency POs during month-end. Please read the short note and update your renewal workflow. Link: https://confluence.redwood/finance/renewal-po-update :loudspeaker:

Diego (Procurement): TL;DR: new rule - any subscription renewal invoiced > $3k requires an issued PO before payment. Pre-approved vendors under $15k still get expedited review but need a PO. See checklist on Confluence.

Hannah (Eng): For context, we often take advantage of annual pricing by paying yearly. If the annual invoice is $10k but monthly-equivalent is <$1k, does the PO rule still apply?

Elena (Finance): Yes. PO rule is based on invoice amount unless you get explicit Procurement exception. Annual $10k invoice needs a PO before paying. If you want to request exception (e.g., annual discount), open a ticket and include cost rationale.

Carla (Legal): Note: any renewal that modifies indemnity, data access, or requires new subprocessors must be routed to Legal regardless of dollar threshold. Mark the procurement ticket with "Legal Review" if unsure.

procurement-bot: New auto-check: when creating a renewal ticket, system will return vendor status (pre-approved | requires-review) and required docs checklist. Missing items will auto-return the ticket. (ID: PROC-2026-05-26)

Diego (Procurement): Onboarding SLA reminder: standard onboarding = 3-5 business days after all docs received. Expedited requests: add "EXPEDITE" tag and justification; we'll triage but cannot guarantee same-day.

Hannah (Eng): Any changes to virtual-card usage? Our infra team uses short-lived cards for cloud provider incident purchases sometimes under $2k.

Elena (Finance): Virtual-card guidance unchanged for one-off operational purchases under $2k. For recurring charges, virtual-card auto-approval is for recurring amounts <$1k/month. All virtual-card requests still follow the PO/approval path when required.

Diego (Procurement): Quick checklist highlight: always attach last executed contract, renewal quote, and vendor tax form. Not attaching these is the most common reason tickets are returned.

Hannah (Eng): Got it. Can procurement-bot expose whether a vendor is on the pre-approved list at ticket creation? That would save back-and-forth.

procurement-bot: Yes. Bot responds with vendor_pre_approval_status and list reference when the vendor field is set.

Elena (Finance): Action items: teams with >$20k/year SaaS spend should schedule a 15-minute sync with Procurement this quarter. Procurement will help map renewals to fiscal months to avoid surprises. If you need a walkthrough of the new flow, reply here with preferred times.

Diego (Procurement): If anyone hits edge cases, open a ticket with subject "PROCURE-ESCALATE" and tag @Diego. We'll review exceptions case-by-case.

Hannah (Eng): Thanks. We'll add the checklist to our Ops runbook.

Elena (Finance): Thanks everyone. We'll post a short FAQ and a recorded walkthrough by EOD Friday. :white_check_mark:
